messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 5032108765 - P95/P99 latency spike detected in shared-gpu-pool-3 streaming tier. p95=1.8s -> 4.2s, p99=3.4s -> 12.6s, error rate steady. Auto-thresholds crossed for streaming_route=/v1/stream and route=/chat/stream. Investigate.
oncall_anna: ack — I'm on it. pulling traces and checking pool-level telemetry.
mike_runtime: linking dashboards: <https://internal.metrics/redwood/pools/shared-gpu-pool-3|shared-gpu-pool-3 metrics> — tail latency jump correlates with disk io wait on hosts 10.2.5.12 & 10.2.5.13, NVMe queue depth near 100%. streaming worker slots saturated.
luis_sre: any noisy tenants pinned to those hosts? run `redwoodctl tenants top` shows big writers. can someone run iostat and `nvml` checks?
oncall_anna: running quick checks: ```
# on 10.2.5.12
iostat -x 1 3
# shows %util ~ 98 for nvme0n1
sudo iotop -aoPa | head -n 10
# top processes are tenant-runtime pid 4472 (tenant: demo-inc) doing large checkpoint writes
nvidia-smi dmon -s u
# GPU util OK, but host io is the hotspot
```
mike_runtime: stack traces for /v1/stream show lots of stalls waiting on disk IO while flushing KV cache segments. KV cache writeback bursting due to big inference sessions from tenant demo-inc.
jess_prod: quick customer check: demo-inc and acme-analytics are the only external tenants with streaming sessions hitting >100 concurrent streams right now. support_bot, any open CS tickets?
support_bot: jira RED-1289 and RED-1290 created minutes ago from monitoring alerts. demo-inc support contact reached out via email reporting slow responses for their interactive demo.
luis_sre: mitigation options: 1) temporarily deprioritize IO for offending tenant via cgroup blkio weight, 2) evict long-lived sessions for that tenant to dedicated pool, 3) throttle streaming concurrency at router layer for tenant until stable. recommendation: cgroup weight + router throttle as immediate action.
oncall_anna: I can apply cgroup tweak now. running: ```
sudo cgget -r blkio.weight /sys/fs/cgroup/tenants/demo-inc || true
sudo cgcreate -g blkio:tenants/demo-inc
# reduce weight to 100 (default 500)
echo 100 | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/tenants/demo-inc/blkio.weight
```
mike_runtime: also push a quick routing rule: ```
# redwoodctl quick-throttle
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/stream --tenant demo-inc --concurrency-limit 40 --reason "mitigate io saturation"
```
oncall_anna: applied cg tweak on 10.2.5.12/13 and pushed router throttle. watching metrics. initial readouts: p99 dropped from 12.6s -> 3.1s within 45s. p95 -> 1.5s.
jess_prod: good. can we reduce customer impact further? any risk to their workloads from cg change?
luis_sre: cg tweak lowers IO share; their long-running checkpoint writes will slow but correctness unaffected. we should proactively notify demo-inc that we'll be throttling throughput to stabilize platform and offer to migrate heavy jobs to dedicated.
support_bot: drafting message: "We detected elevated latency impacting interactive demos and applied temporary throttling to stabilize service. We're offering a migration path to dedicated capacity to avoid future interruptions." want to send after 10m confirmation.
mike_runtime: follow-up actions: - collect kernel blkio stats and nvme queue traces for postmortem - run `kv-cache` eviction profile to avoid writeback spikes - add route-level prefix cache to reduce writeback if possible.
oncall_anna: handing off live monitoring to @luis_sre for the next 30 minutes. If p99 > 5s or error rate increases by >0.5%, page paging@eng-oncall.
luis_sre: ack, I'm taking over live watch. setting grafana alert to conservative thresholds and will keep console updates.
jess_prod: customer impact note for postmortem: affected tenants: demo-inc (major), acme-analytics (minor). windows: 11:04–11:10 UTC mitigation window initial, 11:10–11:20 stabilization. we may offer 5% credit for the 6 minutes of severe degradation.
mike_runtime: small snippet of ps output captured: ```
PID   USER       COMMAND
4472  tenantd    /opt/tenantd/bin/tenant-runtime --tenant demo-inc --checkpoint /var/lib/tenant/checkpoint --batching=on
4520  tenantd    /opt/tenantd/bin/tenant-runtime --tenant acme-analytics --stream
```
luis_sre: creating incident ticket RED-1301 and attaching temporary mitigation steps + commands ran. will include recommended long-term fix: move heavy checkpoint writes off shared nvme to dedicated burst pool or object storage; implement tenant IO QoS via kernel-level weights and admission control at router.
oncall_anna: posting interim status: :white_check_mark: mitigation applied (cg weight + router throttle). metrics improving; continuing monitoring.
jess_prod: scope for follow-up: - schedule migration uplift for demo-inc to dedicated capacity (solutions eng) - add runbook step to detect KV cache writeback spikes and auto-throttle tenant - customer comms template ready.
support_bot: sent initial notice to demo-inc support contact. awaiting reply.
luis_sre: handoff complete to eng-oncall for longer-term cleanup — @eng-oncall please pick up: collect logs from 10.2.5.12/13, verify no residual background writeback, roll back cg tweaks only after sustained 10m stable window.
incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE 5032108765 - mitigation: cgroup blkio weight applied and router throttle active. p99 down to 2.9s, error rate unchanged. Monitor for 15m then move to mitigated.
jess_prod: thanks team. I'll own the customer follow-up and postmortem. please add any missed notes to RED-1301.
luis_sre: logging final note before watch: we should evaluate adding NVMe bandwidth quotas per-tenant if this repeats. will add to backlog.
end of thread
